purpose: Closed vocabulary for synthetic Qwen3-TTS blueprints. Acoustic identity and textual speech style are separately classified; every value is closed, evidenced, and rendered deterministically.

models.rule: VoiceDesign only produces reference clips. Dialogue lines are always generated by the Base model with a cached ICL prompt. Mood never reaches the Base model as text.

reference.text: Good evening. The road ahead is quiet tonight, although the weather may change before morning. Keep to the marked path, and listen for the bells. Have you brought everything you need?
rules: Every character and every mood uses this exact text. A shared script makes voices comparable and keeps ICL extraction uniform.
Do not translate, trim, or personalize the script per character.
Reject a recording shorter than 8 s or longer than 18 s; regenerate with the same seed offset instead of editing the audio.
Store the exact transcript with every generated clip; ICL requires ref_text to match the audio word for word.
The open-weight model has a reported ICL startup artifact where the first words of the reference leak into the output. Check the first 2 s of a new profile before approving it.

presentation.question: How is the voice heard, not what the character's body or gender identity is?

masculine.notes: A deliberate synthetic vocal presentation; game sex metadata may inform a creative choice but is never acoustic evidence.

feminine.notes: A deliberate synthetic vocal presentation; game sex metadata may inform a creative choice but is never acoustic evidence.

androgynous.notes: Deliberately ambiguous presentation; choose only as a marked synthetic casting decision or when a source explicitly describes it.

neutral.notes: Minimal gender cue. Useful for narrators, generic voices, and characters whose vocal presentation is unstated.

nonhuman.notes: Beast, lifeless, or ethereal timbre. Experimental: Qwen3-TTS is a speech model and may render this as an odd human voice. Always audition.

synthetic.notes: Mammets, nodes, Allagan constructs. Experimental, audition required.

perceived_age.question: How old does the voice sound, not how old the character is in lore years?

youthful.range: childlike or young-teen impression; no precise age claim

notes: Use perceived vocal age. A 100-year-old Elezen may sound like a young adult; a 30-year-old Lalafell still sounds adult, never childlike.
Null is allowed and preferred over a guess. The renderer simply omits the age clause.
Never combine an age with a presentation that contradicts it (child + mature); one value only by construction.
Register describes where the voice sits, not how expressive it is.
Body size and race are not sufficient evidence for a register; they are at most creative_selection.
Extreme ends (very_low, very_high) require explicit or supported_inference evidence.
Optional. Omit when unsure; the model defaults to a natural range.

perceived_vocal_size.question: How large does the voice sound?
notes: A deliberate synthetic-casting descriptor, not a measured formant scale or vocal-tract length.
Derived only from documented race/clan morphology; never from height sliders until race+gender ranges are validated.
Omit when there is no recognized morphology prior.

vocal_weight.question: How full or light does the voice sound?
notes: A deliberate synthetic-casting descriptor, not vocal-fold mass, loudness, or a measured acoustic property.
Muscle tone may add at most a very weak weight cue for validated model combinations.
Omit when there is no recognized morphology prior.

timbre_primary.question: What is the dominant texture of the voice?
notes: This is the single most differentiating field after pitch. Spend the creative effort here.
Values that share a family are acoustically redundant; the validator rejects combining two of them (husky + gravelly is one instruction, not two).
At most one secondary texture, from a different family than the primary.
Two overlapping roughness words muddle the instruction; three guarantee mush.
Preferred secondary use is a light modifier: slightly breathy, slightly nasal, a hint of reediness.
Audit list of the supported timbre preferences behind timbre_primary and timbre_secondary.
Derived weakly from perceived vocal size/weight; never a forced race timbre or resonance placement.
Optional. Omit rather than guess; a wrong resonance clause is a bigger error than a missing one.
How consonants and vowels are formed. Default for ordinary NPCs is relaxed or crisp.
slurred, drawling, staccato, and sharp are acting choices and require explicit or supported_inference evidence.
Pace is a rhythm property of the voice, not an emotion. An angry character is not automatically fast.
measured and moderate cover most NPCs; very_slow and very_fast need evidence.
Default natural. Prefer natural or restrained; dramatic and melodic make a character's every line theatrical.
Personality traits such as stoic or arrogant may justify restrained, but only as supported_inference.
Profile and strength are set together or both omitted; the validator rejects half an accent.
Qwen3-TTS has no accent mode. Accent clauses are soft hints; verify by listening before approving a profile.
Never derive an accent from a nation or race alone. Use the project default when the wiki says nothing.
The project default is evidence level 'default', never 'explicit'.
Embellishments, never mandatory. Omit most of the time.
A trait whose family matches an already selected timbre, resonance, or articulation is redundant and is rejected.

render.style_note: Rendered only from Style fields with status supported (including fields whose value is mixed); provisional, insufficient, unresolved, and rejected fields are omitted. The Identity sentence stays byte-identical when Style changes.
render.article_rule: Use 'An' when the rendered phrase starts with a vowel sound (adult, ageless, ancient, elderly, androgynous), otherwise 'A'.
render.banned_identity_words_reason: Identity is the constant; emotion belongs to the mood layer. An emotion word in the identity prompt makes every line of the character permanently emotional.
render.word_target_note: 48 is the hard ceiling: it still fits accent plus secondary timbre plus two traits. Anything longer dilutes the description, and Qwen's own voice-design examples are shorter.

values.explicit: A source directly describes this audible quality or factual field; retain its exact supporting quote and provenance.
values.supported_inference: Multiple attributed source statements support this value; retain the relevant source quotes and provenance.
values.creative_selection: A deliberate synthetic casting decision, not a claim about an original recording or actor.
values.default: A named project fallback from this vocabulary; not source evidence.
values.unknown: Insufficient reliable information; optional fields remain null.

rules: Every non-null acoustic identity field has one evidence record.
explicit and supported_inference require source URL or game-data identifier, source type, and exact short quote.
creative_selection and default are clearly labelled and must not impersonate source facts.
unknown is valid only for nullable fields.
Race, clan, sex, body, occupation, and personality cannot be acoustic evidence.

allowed: An explicit source description of audible qualities can support the matching closed acoustic field.
Dialogue measurements can support speech-style classification only; they do not establish pitch, timbre, resonance, articulation, or accent.
Race, clan, sex, body, age appearance, occupation, and personality may be considered only as creative context and must be labeled creative_selection, never as acoustic fact.
A stated lore age may be recorded as lore metadata; do not convert species lifespan to perceived vocal age.
forbidden: Race, clan, sex, height, build, or body mass as evidence for pitch, timbre, resonance, articulation, pace, or accent.
Occupation as evidence for timbre or pitch (a craft role does not make a voice gravelly).
Personality as evidence for pitch, timbre, resonance, age, or accent (cheerfulness does not mean high pitch).
Dialogue-derived vocabulary complexity or sentence length as evidence of articulation, accent, pitch, or timbre.
Mood words as permanent identity fields.
Adding emotion to the identity prompt because a character is usually emotional.
Inventing lore facts, acoustic evidence, or source quotations.
inference_policy.required_for_allowed_inferences: Every audible selection without an exact source quote is creative_selection or default. Creative casting is not a claim about an original actor.

profile_rules: One canonical profile per NPC id. Labels that resolve to the same NPC share the profile.
Unnamed or generic labels get a bank archetype profile, not a new invented voice.
A character profile never stores audio, seeds, or paths; reference recordings and cached prompts live in the generated voice directory.
profiles are versioned; bump profile_version whenever a selected value changes, so already-generated lines can be traced to the voice that produced them.

checks: reference_duration_ok: the neutral clip is 10-15 s.
reference_transcript_verified: the stored transcript matches the audio word for word.
no_reference_leak: the first 2 s of a held-out clone do not repeat the reference tail.
identity_approved: a human listened and accepted the voice as the character.
no_drift: two independent clone lines are recognisably the same speaker.

speech_style.purpose: Closed classification of a character’s recurring written-dialogue style. Style is separate from acoustic Identity and is appended only when supported by dialogue evidence.

register.question: What register best describes the dialogue wording?

formal.classification_description: Consistently ceremonial or official grammar and address forms; vocabulary complexity and contractions are judged separately.

neutral.classification_description: Ordinary grammatical register with no sustained ceremonial or casual stance.

conversational.classification_description: Consistently casual grammar and address forms; do not infer this from contractions or slang alone.

mixed.classification_description: Formality shifts with a stable contextual rule, such as formal address in one setting and casual grammar in another.

lexical_complexity.question: How lexically complex is the character’s word choice, independent of subject matter?

plain.classification_description: Mostly high-frequency concrete words; lexical rarity only, not sentence length.

ordinary.classification_description: Everyday range of high- and mid-frequency words with no sustained difficult vocabulary.

advanced.classification_description: Frequent less-common words across topics; technical, poetic, archaic and dialectal choices are separate audit features, not complexity levels.

mixed.classification_description: Two complexity levels recur in distinct, stable contexts.

sentence_complexity.question: How structurally complex are the sampled utterances?

simple.classification_description: Sustained single-clause grammar; length alone does not make structure complex.

mixed.classification_description: Single- and multi-clause grammar both recur without one clearly dominating.

complex.classification_description: Subordination or coordinated clauses recur as the normal structure.

colloquialism.question: How often does the dialogue use colloquial wording?

low.classification_description: Nonstandard or slang forms are rare across contexts; contractions alone do not raise this field.

moderate.classification_description: Nonstandard or slang forms recur but do not dominate ordinary lines.

high.classification_description: Nonstandard or slang forms are the normal lexical choice across contexts.

mixed.classification_description: Nonstandard forms are sustained in one context and absent in another.

discourse_style.question: What recurring way does the character organize and direct discourse?

direct.classification_description: Claims and requests are stated without hedging, framing, or extended setup.

explanatory.classification_description: The recurring move is to explain causes, sequences, or conditions so the listener understands.

inquisitive.classification_description: The recurring move is asking questions rather than asserting.

persuasive.classification_description: The recurring move is to argue for a course of action with reasons or appeals.

exhortative.classification_description: The recurring move is to urge, command, or rally the listener toward action.

reflective.classification_description: The recurring move is to weigh uncertainty, memory, or inner conflict rather than settle a claim.

narrative.classification_description: The recurring move is to recount events in sequence as a story.

mixed.classification_description: Two or more discourse moves recur in distinct, stable contexts.

speech_habits.question: Which repeated textual speech habits occur in the sample?

signals.dialect_note: Dialect and archaic address forms. They weight which lines are sampled and are counted for the model, but they are deliberately NOT part of the formal/colloquial rate: 'ye' and 'pray' are archaic, not informal, and folding them into the register measurement would corrupt it.

speech_style.measurement_rules: dialogue.py calculates measurements and sample pools only. RulesProvider is an explicit baseline; it is never a hidden fallback or ground truth. Production labels come from evidence-backed JEV or an explicitly selected rules baseline.

sufficiency.note: Initial floors from the v2 annotation protocol; tune only on development data.

classification.provider_contract: RulesProvider is an explicitly selected offline baseline and never a fallback. JevProvider sends one identity-blind System One request for the five Style dimensions. JEV output must cite supplied line IDs; model confidence is diagnostic only.

speech_style.register.instructions: Which register does the character habitually use across ordinary dialogue? Use mixed for recurring shifts and abstain when the sample is too sparse.

speech_style.lexical_complexity.instructions: How difficult is the character's habitual word choice? Judge lexical rarity only, not sentence length, technical topic, poetry, archaism, dialect, intelligence, education, or class; proper names and quest terms are not advanced vocabulary.

speech_style.sentence_complexity.instructions: What sentence structures does the character habitually use? Normalize concatenated fragments before judging.

speech_style.colloquialism.instructions: How frequently does the character use informal spoken-language forms across contexts?

speech_style.discourse_style.instructions: What recurring way does the character organize discourse: state, explain, question, persuade, urge, reflect, or narrate? This is written discourse, not vocal speed, loudness, or emotion.

confidence_policy: Model self-reported confidence/probability is diagnostic metadata, never calibrated production confidence.
Acceptance depends on valid labels, cited line IDs present in the request, sample sufficiency, stability, and held-out benchmark metrics.
RulesProvider results are recorded as method=rules_baseline and are never merged into JEV fields.
A field below the minimum evidence floor is null with status=insufficient_evidence; no first-option or neutral default is inserted.
Status describes evidence sufficiency only. mixed is a classification value, never a status; a mixed value uses status supported or provisional.
Unresolved evidence yields null with status=unresolved.
Thresholds and evidence floors are initial project settings and must be calibrated on development data only.
classification.acoustic_family_compatibility: Primary and optional secondary timbres must use different acoustic families. Distinctive traits cannot repeat the selected primary family.
classification.speech_style_separation: Speech-style results stay out of the identity prompt and never become acoustic evidence.

profile_lifecycle.approval_rule: Only a human review action may set approved. Classification confidence and human approval are separate fields.

schema_migrations.1.0_to_1.1: Adds speech-style classifications, lifecycle and classification provenance. Existing identity selections and the Qwen reference script keep their original meanings. Use the explicit blueprint migration command; old profiles are never silently rewritten.
schema_migrations.reference_script_policy: The schema 1.0 npc_reference_v1 script remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
schema_migrations.1.1_to_1.2: Removes the mood/archon layer and the wiki-derived lore fields. Profiles keep identity, speech style, lifecycle and evidence unchanged; migration is explicit.
